about: History's state monopolies (the Ledger topic 'Treasury and money', decisions 'How a monopoly works' and 'Which goods can be monopolised'): each good a state alone could sell, the realms (start_realms keys) that held it, the years, and the source. A realm may declare these easily in their years; any other good it makes can be declared too, at more anger. 'farmed': history let contractors run it. Later-era realm keys are listed for when those realms come into the game. Our own data, free for any use.

monopolies.source: The Revenue Laws of Ptolemy II (P. Rev., 259 BC): the crown alone pressed and sold oil, at fixed prices, through contractors.
The Revenue Laws of Ptolemy II (P. Rev., 259 BC) cover sesame, castor and other oil crops with olive oil.
Papyrus was a royal sale under the Ptolemies (P. Tebt. 308; Pliny, Natural History 13.70 on its trade).
Royal weaving workshops and fixed linen deliveries (P. Rev. cols. 87-107; P. Tebt. 5).
The beer monopoly (zytera) was farmed out under the Ptolemies (P. Tebt. 40).
The Ptolemaic salt tax (halike) and royal salt sales (P. Tebt. 1, 5).
Natron was a farmed royal monopoly (P. Tebt. 40; P. Rev.).
The censors of 204 BC fixed the price of salt in Rome and Italy (Livy 29.37); the salt works were let to publicani.
The Seleucid salt tax, remitted to the Jews by Demetrius I (1 Maccabees 10.29, 11.35).
Frankincense could be brought only to Sabota, the Hadramite capital, where the king took his tithe; leaving the road was a capital crime (Pliny, Natural History 12.63).
Justinian made silk a state monopoly (Procopius, Secret History 25).
Emperor Wu's salt and iron monopolies, 117 BC (Sima Qian, Shiji 30; the Discourses on Salt and Iron, 81 BC).
Emperor Wu's salt and iron monopolies, 117 BC (Sima Qian, Shiji 30).
The Venetian Salt Office (Camera del Sal), which controlled the salt trade of the Adriatic.
The gabelle, made permanent in 1341 and farmed to the Ferme générale from 1681; abolished in 1790.
The Castilian tobacco monopoly (estanco del tabaco), 1636.
The East India Company's Bengal opium monopoly, 1773.
